common_name: Blue Wonder Catmint (Compact Sterile Hybrid Catmint)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in lean, gritty, well-drained soil in full sun; Blue Wonder is a sterile Faassen Nurseries selection bred for larger-than-typical flowers on a compact mound.

directions: Blue Wonder forms a tidy, rounded mound of soft silver-blue foliage topped by lavender-blue flower spikes noticeably larger than those of most other faassenii-type catmints, blooming from late spring through summer. Because it is a sterile hybrid it channels its energy into an extended bloom period rather than seed production, and it will not self-sow into surrounding beds. Shear the mound back lightly after the first flush fades to keep the habit dense and to encourage a second round of bloom into fall. Once established it shrugs off heat and drought and draws a steady stream of bees and butterflies.

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Superba forms a low, mat-like clump of dwarf raceme catmint useful for edging and rock gardens.

directions: Superba spreads into a fine-textured, mat-forming clump of small aromatic silver-green leaves, sending up upright stems of violet-blue flowers from late spring through the autumn. Its compact, low habit sets it apart from taller catmints and suits it well to border edges, rock gardens, and containers where a sprawling cultivar would overwhelm its neighbors. Shear the plant back by about a third after the first bloom flush to tidy the mound and prompt continued flowering into fall. It is highly drought-tolerant once established and is rarely troubled by deer or rabbits.

common_name: Little Trudy Catmint (Extra-Compact Plant Select Catmint)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Little Trudy is a 2008 Plant Select award-winning Colorado selection bred to be the most compact catmint available.

directions: Little Trudy builds a dense, low mound of serrated silvery foliage covered in lavender flowers with a distinct pink tinge, blooming almost continuously from spring until frost. Selected at Little Valley Wholesale Nursery in Colorado, it is the smallest widely available catmint cultivar, making it well suited to bed edges, containers, and rock gardens where larger Nepeta would crowd out neighboring plants. It is sterile and will not seed around the garden, though it slowly naturalizes into a broader clump over time. Deer and rabbits generally avoid it, and bees visit its long bloom season heavily.

common_name: Felix Catmint (Compact Deep Mauve-Blue Dwarf Catmint)

planting.note: Plant container divisions in spring in dry to average, well-drained soil in full sun or part shade; Felix is a compact, floriferous dwarf catmint suited to small-space plantings.

directions: Felix forms a uniform, compact mound of felty gray-green leaves set off by deep lilac-blue, two-lipped tubular flowers that appear abundantly from May into October. Its neat, low habit and long bloom season make it a reliable front-of-border or rock garden plant that rarely needs staking. Cutting the plant back after the first flush of bloom keeps the mound tidy and encourages a strong second flowering later in the season. It tolerates dry, average soils once established and is a dependable honeybee forage plant that deer tend to avoid.

common_name: Grand Parade Bee Balm (Compact Mildew-Resistant Morden Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in consistently moist, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Grand Parade ('ACrade') is a Morden Research Station introduction bred for cold hardiness and powdery mildew resistance.

directions: Grand Parade produces an abundance of lavender-purple flower heads atop mint-scented foliage on mid-sized, well-branched plants that hold their shape without flopping. Bred at Manitoba's Morden Breeding Program, it carries markedly improved resistance to the powdery mildew that commonly disfigures older bee balm selections by late summer. Bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds visit the nectar-rich blooms heavily from mid- to late summer. Deadhead spent flower heads to prolong bloom and divide congested clumps every few years in early spring to maintain vigor and air circulation.

common_name: Leading Lady Razzberry Bee Balm (Petite Early-Blooming Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in rich, moist, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Leading Lady Razzberry (PP34130) is a Walters Gardens introduction bred for an extra-compact, non-running habit and early bloom.

directions: Leading Lady Razzberry bears bright raspberry-purple tubular flowers arranged in dense whorls above dark green, purple-tinged foliage and dark bracts, blooming earlier than most bee balms from early into midsummer on plants that stay under about a foot tall. Its petite, well-behaved clump does not spread by runners the way many Monarda do, making it a good fit for borders and containers where space is limited. The aromatic foliage is naturally deer resistant, while the sweet nectar draws butterflies, hummingbirds, and honeybees throughout its bloom window. Divide clumps every few years in early spring to keep plants vigorous.
